item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Aug 18 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Aug 18 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Aug 18 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Tue Aug 18, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: John Waldron Arts Centere — Tue Aug 18, 2:00 PM — ids@iu.edu
item.description:
date/time: 8/16-8/26 @ 2pm and 7pm Love is never simple. At least it's funny. Starring Bloomington's favorite acting duo - Valerie C. Kilmer & Bobby Ayala Perez! In this clever \(and extremely funny\) play about relationships, five couples explore the delights and disappointments of their sex lives. Whether they are the first two people on Earth or the last two, modern partners with shifting needs, exes on the eve of a life-altering event, or twelfth-century pen pals, following those most natural desires uncovers truths about their humanity. Chiara Atik's Five Times in One Night is a hilarious examination of intimacy through the ages. "A sharp, witty meditation on relationships through time." - Stage Buddy "One of the most thoroughly entertaining, original, and enjoyable shows I've seen." -This Week in New York Age Recommendation: 18\+
Source: Limestone Post

item.title: CANCELLED: Tuesday Market at Hopewell Commons — Tue Aug 18, 4:00 PM — Hopewell Commons
item.description:
Find more information about the Tuesday Market at https://bloomington.in.gov/farmers-market/tuesdayThe Tuesday Market takes place rain or shine every Tuesday, June through September, at Hopewell Commons, 630 S. Morton St. in BloomingtonThe Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. Food and beverage artisans provide a tasteful variety of drinks, pastries, and savory dishes. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.
Source: Parks and Recreation

item.title: IU Cinema: Legally Blonde — Tue Aug 18, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Welcome a brand-new school year with the whip-smart comedic chops of Witherspoon, Wilson, Coolidge, and more! What, like it's hard? Not with this set of legal eagles! 25th anniversary screening.
Elle Woods (Reese Witherspoon) is a California blonde with couture clothes (mostly pink, obvs), fabulous friends, and the hottest boyfriend on campus. So when Warner Huntington III (Matthew Davis) suddenly dumps her and heads to Harvard Law School, Elle takes matters into her own manicured hands and enrolls as well. Now, getting Warner back should be a snap (well, maybe a bend and snap), right? Wrong! Elle's about to begin the toughest fight of her life ... for love, honor, justice, and respect for blondes everywhere! Luke Wilson, Selma Blair, Victor Garber, Holland Taylor, and Jennifer Coolidge round out a fantastic ensemble cast. item.description:
Meredith Funeral Home, in partnership with the historic Brown County Playhouse, is excited to offer a Free Monthly Movie Series for those aged 60 and over. Enjoy a classic film with friends, free popcorn, and a soda—all in the comfort of the historic Brown County Playhouse!
When: AUG 20, 2026 – The Princess Bride Time: 2:00 p.m. Doors open at 1:00 p.m. Where: Historic Brown County Playhouse, 70 S Van Buren St. in Nashville, IN No ticket is necessary, and admission is free for those 60 and over. For those under 60, admission is just $7.
This initiative is part of the Meredith family’s ongoing commitment to giving back to the community. Bill and Jamie Meredith, along with their dedicated staff, are excited to create a monthly opportunity for seniors to connect with others and enjoy a time of fellowship. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Aug 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Aug 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Aug 24 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.description:

Morton St. in BloomingtonThe Market is a gathering place where local farmers, makers, and neighbors come together to share the foods, traditions, and connections that strengthen our community and support a reliable local food supply.Market goers find a wide assortment of goods from the farm and field, including fruits and vegetables, eggs, meats and cheeses, honey, seasonal flowers, and annual and perennial plants. This weekly gathering provides opportunities for individuals to connect with their community in meaningful ways and support local farmers and small businesses.
